findings.finding: Today's peer prints (2026-10-13) landed after BAC last spoke on 2026-09-14: JPM markets +15% to $10.3bn (FICC -4% YoY, equities +49%), IB fees +14%; GS equities +72%, record advisory; this is consistent with BAC's flat-S&T guide (FICC-heavy mix) and gives modest room for equities to carry S&T to or slightly above the guide, but BAC's IB guide (-10%+ YoY) is company-specific and peers do not overturn it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BAC fell >5% (to $59.48 from $62.69) on 2026-09-14 when it guided S&T flat and IB $1.6-1.8bn; on the Q2 2026 print (S&T ex-DVA +33%) the stock rose +1.82%/+1.88% around the April and July prints per baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market sold BAC 5% on the guide and the peer equities boom was visible intraday today; if the market expected BAC to beat its own S&T guide the stock would have recovered toward the $59 post-guide level rather than falling another ~9%. Lands inside the company's own guide, so sized near zero.
findings.independence: JPM markets detail from Quartz (snippet only, https://qz.com/jpmorgan-chase-q3-2026-earnings-miss-analyst-estimates-101326) and JPM's 8-K supplement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfex992supplement.htm, IB fees $2,960m vs $2,612m). Different documents from the 247wallst GS figures.

findings.finding: Peer reaction function today favours the de-risked: JPM missed EPS ($5.57 vs ~$5.75-5.93) yet rose ~0.8-1%, XLF +1%, while BAC enters with its capital-markets weakness pre-announced and a ~16% one-month drawdown (RSI ~25), so the print's bad lines are largely in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 3 of last 4 prints up (+4.37, +1.82, +1.88, one -3.78 in Jan 2026); median |move| 2.83%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had already discounted that pre-announced weakness is behind it, BAC would not be sitting at $53.9 near its support with a one-month -16% while XLF rallied on peer prints; the counterweight (WFC sold -1.5 to -3% for NII lagging 11% balance growth, a story BAC shares) is netted into this size.
findings.independence: TradingKey 2026-10-11 (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262208414-bank-of-america-bac-stock-forecast-october-11-2026-tradingkey) on RSI ~25 and the drawdown; Motley Fool 2026-10-12 on the -16% month. Same-day peer moves also in 247wallst (shared fact base with finding 1, but different line).

findings.finding: NII guidance read-through is steady-to-firm: WFC held FY2026 NII ~$50bn with a Q4 step-up to ~$13bn from $12.5bn, JPM guided Q4 NII ex-markets ~$25.5bn and 2027 ~$107bn with forward rate hikes contributing; BAC's top-of-6-8% guide assumed one 2026 hike, already delivered in September, and its disclosed +100bp sensitivity is ~+$1bn, so a firmed Q4/2027 NII outlook is the likelier direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NII +9%, FY guide raised to top of 6-8%): stock +1.88% per baseline and described as 'flatlining' by TIKR; NII is the line the stock is said to trade on now (Motley Fool 2026-10-12).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen on 'higher rates hurt banks' (Motley Fool 2026-10-12) while BAC is asset-sensitive; if the NII upside from the hike path were priced BAC would not have underperformed through a hike its own guide assumed. Proxy from peers, so sized small; WFC's deposit cost +5bp QoQ is the counterweight and is netted in.
findings.independence: JPM call highlights (https://marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-jpmorgan-chase-co-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-13/?amp=) and BAC's own guide basis in Motley Fool (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/12/is-bank-of-america-s-stock-a-buy-ahead-of-its-q3-earnings-report-on-oct-14/).

findings.finding: BAC's own card master trust is clean into the quarter: BA Credit Card Trust August 2026 annualised net charge-offs 2.15% (2.13% Jul, 2.23% Jun) and 60+ delinquency 0.89% vs 0.95% in May; peers concur (JPM card NCO guide held ~3.2%, WFC card NCOs lower).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been a surprise line for BAC in the last four prints; previews call it benign.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: consensus already expects benign credit. Filed because it is a company-level primary number, sized near zero since it confirms rather than contradicts expectations.
findings.independence: JPM card NCO guide (marketbeat, above) and WFC consumer NCOs (investing.com, above).

findings.finding: Rates on the balance sheet are a live negative for the capital line: the Fed hiked in September and 10/30-year yields reached multi-year highs, JPM took $658m of net investment securities losses that caused its EPS miss and GS's CET1 fell to 12.4%; BAC's large securities book means wider AOCI/HTM marks and a risk of a slower buyback or a similar securities-loss headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved BAC print in the baseline turned on capital return; JPM rose ~1% today despite the securities-loss miss, which shrinks this.
findings.why_not_priced: Yields are public, so the macro is priced; what is not is whether BAC repositions or slows buybacks. Inference from peers, not confirmed by BAC, so small; short interest 1.4% means no squeeze offset needed.
findings.independence: Fortune 2026-10-13 on the September hike and yields (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/); 247wallst on GS CET1 12.4%.
